summary: Assess electrical AI use cases, data readiness, and model outputs through practical engineering exercises. Review the course and build decision-ready artefacts.
lede: Artificial intelligence for electrical engineering helps teams assess how data can support maintenance and power-system decisions. For electrical engineers, asset specialists, and power-system professionals, the course focuses on evaluating practical AI use cases rather than building production models. You will frame use cases with CRISP-DM, check data readiness, and interpret predictive-maintenance and load-forecasting outputs, while considering uncertainty and operational risks.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who evaluate electrical equipment, power-system performance, or engineering data and need to assess where AI can support a practical operational decision.
modules: Electrical AI Use Cases and CRISP-DM
NIST AI Risk Management for Electrical Systems
Engineering Decision Reporting and AI Roadmaps
prerequisites: Working knowledge of electrical engineering, power systems, or electrical asset operations is recommended. No programming is required for course completion; exercises focus on use-case assessment, spreadsheet-based data review, and interpretation of AI outputs.
topics: Data science & machine learning in practice
